Subject: MAP kickoff — contracting owners, evaluation plan, and term clearance

Hi Diane / Acme Procurement team,

Thanks for the productive pilot discussions last week. To keep momentum, I want to start a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) focused on three immediate areas: (1) contracting owners and redline cadence, (2) the evaluation plan and success criteria for your pilot, and (3) a realistic close timeline so we can align internal approvals.

Attached is a draft MAP workbook (MAP_v1.xlsx) with milestones and a proposed 6-week timetable. High-level asks from us to you:
- Confirm the single terms owner for commercial/legal redlines (name + email)
- Confirm procurement intake steps and expected review SLAs (e.g., legal review in 5 business days)
- Confirm evaluation criteria and which internal stakeholders will sign acceptance (performance, privacy, integration)

Proposed owners on the Redwood side:
- Marissa Cole — commercial lead (pricing & SOW)
- Ben Carter — solutions/technical evaluation coordinator
- Connor O'Brien — customer success / onboarding lead
- Soojin Lee — legal-routing and program lead for this MAP

If Diane can confirm the Acme terms owner and a preferred redline process (DocuSign/Share redline/markups in PDF), we’ll lock the milestones and schedule a 30-minute cadence starting next week.

Thanks — happy to adjust the timeline if you have procurement windows to account for.

Best,

Soojin Lee
Head of Contracts & Programs
Redwood Inference

Thanks Soojin — this is helpful.

Quick notes from procurement/legal:
- Primary terms owner will be Ted Lawson (cc'd) from Orbis (our outsourced legal). Ted's inbox is ted.lawson@orbishealth.com.
- Our procurement team prefers markups in a redline PDF; we track critical issues in our intake form.
- Typical SLAs: initial commercial review (3 business days), legal redline backlog (up to 7 business days depending on complexity).

For evaluation: we'll run a 3-week pilot with a core clinical group and an internal data science check. Acceptance will require: no PHI exfiltration, latency < 250ms 95th percentile on a 1k-sample, and documentation of model provenance. I'll add the names of the clinical leads by EOD.

Can we get a simple redline guide or preferred clause language from Redwood for our legal team to review? Also please include a visible path for regulatory evidence (SOC2 scope, data retention, audit logging).

Regards,
Diane
Director, Clinical Platforms
Acme Health
